clue.text: Very keen to stay around conference venue

indicators.note: turned around, so the two words are read backwards together

parts.note: very keen on something means mad about it
to stay is to stop where you are

explanation.surface: Someone eager to remain near the place where a big meeting is being held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns MADSTOP backwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1945 Allied summit that settled post-war Germany was held in this town near Berlin.

clue.text: Spurs No 2 has long throw

indicators.note: number two picks the second letter of the word before it

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A Tottenham Hotspur player wearing the number two shirt has a big throw-in.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch a ball is to throw or hurl it.

clue.text: Start in winding passage

indicators.note: winding means twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin inside a twisting corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges START IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across, so a passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Henry's climbing down over style

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: feeling down means sad
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry descends while climbing, with a flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means flair or panache, a sense of style.

clue.text: Genuine? Hmm! React to "settlement"(of 19 21) …

indicators.note: settlement suggests the letters being settled into a new order, as well as naming the pact

explanation.surface: A sceptical reaction to the deal struck by 19 21, continuing into 5 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 21 is CHAMBERLAIN, the prime minister who signed this 1938 pact with Hitler. 'settlement' rearranges GENUINE HMM REACT and also names the pact.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1938 Munich pact ceded Czech Sudetenland to Germany and was hailed by Chamberlain as peace for our time.

clue.text: Hacked Off, with film star involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: with can mean and, as in 'bread with butter'
Richard Gere, the Hollywood actor

explanation.surface: Suggests the Hacked Off press-reform campaign gaining a celebrity supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Hacked Off is the British campaign group for press regulation backed by celebrities, which makes the capitals look like a name rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling hacked off is British slang for being annoyed or made cross.

clue.text: … that's in force? Please, it's a whopper — scrap!

definitions.text: … that's in force? Please, it's a whopper — scrap!

indicators.note: to scrap something is to break it up, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Continuing 4 down: scepticism that the pact holds, calling it a lie fit to be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' rearranges FORCE PLEASE IT'S A WHOPPER, and the whole clue also describes the 1938 pact, mocked by history as useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamberlain waved the signed paper; it proved valueless when Hitler invaded Czechoslovakia.

clue.text: "Don't stop upsetting party!" — PM receiving one side's cheers

parts.note: keep going, so go

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: Edward Heath was a British Prime Minister
L, left, is one side

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep spoiling a party while the Prime Minister welcomes cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses the party word, and 'receiving' puts L inside the PM; Edward Heath was UK Prime Minister 1970-74.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast drunk to someone's wellbeing, used like the word you say when clinking glasses.

clue.text: Musical genre infuriated man

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay puts a man's name, Tim, in a word for fury: a man in a rage, which is an infuriated man

explanation.surface: A style of music has made a man furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infuriated' does double duty: read as 'in a rage', it supplies both the container and the instruction to put the man inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano style popularised by Scott Joplin, a genre of music.

clue.text: Shows up group (1D)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading backwards

parts.note: a set is a group
read literally as one D

explanation.surface: Appears to be a band, though 1D is the boy band One Direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 1D looks like a cross-reference to 1 down, or the boy band One Direction; it is read as ONE and D. 'up' reverses SETONED.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to indicate or signify, so it shows.

clue.text: Violently attacks stationer after a fracas

indicators.note: after a brawl things are scattered and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who sells pens and paper gets violent once a brawl has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fracas' rearranges the letters of STATIONER.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone with fury or force; a phrasal verb for a fierce assault.

clue.text: What can be played by men on horseback

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
read as horse back: a horse is a NAG, and back turns it round

explanation.surface: A riddle about something cavalrymen can perform on while mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the pieces one after the other; 'horseback' splits into horse (NAG) and back, which reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A church keyboard instrument is something a musician plays.

clue.text: That bloke's southern German

parts.note: that bloke is means he is, contracted to he's

explanation.surface: Pointing out that a certain man is a German from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Hess was a leading Nazi, Hitler's deputy, so a well-known German.

clue.text: Spirit audience's not picked up — it's insubstantial

parts.note: Scotch whisky is a spirit

indicators.note: what an audience hears, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: something not picked up is missed

explanation.surface: A drink goes unnoticed by the listeners, which makes it seem flimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch mist is a fine drizzle, and figuratively anything imaginary or without substance.

clue.text: Jail those selling drugs to clerical people

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure, slang for prison
drug dealers are pushers

explanation.surface: Lock up drug dealers, says someone, aimed at clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clerical' looks like clergy; here it means office clerks.
explanation.definitionFit: Office workers doing routine paperwork, a dismissive term for clerks.

clue.text: One-time female's a divine creature

parts.note: one is A, as in a single thing
a hen is a female bird, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A former woman has become a godlike being.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom is a divine being.

clue.text: Support government resigning — claims they want out

indicators.note: resigning means leaving, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
avers means asserts or claims

explanation.surface: A political row: backing the government while ministers quit, said by those wishing to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in Brexit year: 'they want out' points at people who voted to leave the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: People departing, notably Brexit voters who wished to quit the European Union.

clue.text: See 5 down
Making love shortly after wrestling — animal!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so each word loses its final letter

parts.note: post is Latin for after
sumo is Japanese wrestling

explanation.surface: Someone having sex soon after a wrestling bout — what a beast!
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts both POST and SUMO short, giving POS and SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The American marsupial known for playing dead is a creature.

clue.text: Child's cut not real — point taken

indicators.note: taken in, so the letter goes inside
cut means the end is chopped off

parts.note: pretend means make-believe, not real
E is a compass point

explanation.surface: A child's haircut is fake, and the point has been accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims PRETEND to PRETEN, and 'taken' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A child aged around ten to twelve, just before the teenage years.

clue.text: Comic routine about height in bad taste

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a sick joke is one in bad taste

explanation.surface: A comedian's act concerning tallness is distasteful.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yiddish-derived word for a performer's trademark gimmick or comedy act.

clue.text: House cleaner receives award

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the award goes inside

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour

explanation.surface: A domestic cleaner is given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is a British term for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative chamber, like the Commons, is a house of parliament.

clue.text: Done with PM's backing — Sun perhaps fails to respond to alarm

parts.note: done with means over, finished

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister, so the PM's is Peel's
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: Finished with the Prime Minister's support, a newspaper fails to respond to a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses PEELS to SLEEP. The Sun looks like the tabloid but is just Sunday's S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sleeps past the time they meant to wake has not reacted to their clock's bell.

clue.text: Put down before Indiana city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
IN is the postal abbreviation for Indiana

explanation.surface: Something laid down before a city in Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' sets the city ahead of the state, though the surface makes Indiana the city's home. With 19 it completes the theme's prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of lie: something that has lain has been set or rested down.

clue.text: Wanting help, joint letter said

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the pair is taken by its sound

parts.note: a knee is a joint, and dee is how the letter D is spoken

explanation.surface: A shared letter is described as requiring assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being needy means requiring support or lacking necessities.

clue.text: Married woman's cheating husband finally kicked out

indicators.note: kicked out means removed from the word

parts.note: fraud is cheating or deception

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wife's unfaithful husband is eventually thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German title for a married woman, like Mrs.

clue.text: Jobs lost everywhere? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, so the answer sits inside it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether employment has disappeared all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Jobs' looks like employment; it is Apple founder Steve Jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: First name of the Apple co-founder whose surname is Jobs.

clue.text: Awful from City playing b***** Real

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex-works
EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: a team playing is in action, signalling the letters move about

parts.note: the starred-out swearword shows only its first letter

explanation.surface: A football fan curses dreadful Manchester City playing Real Madrid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges B and REAL into RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means utterly detestable or very bad, a strong synonym.

clue.text: Attitudes accepted by detective in force

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the force

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police force in London
in means accepted or fashionable
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: Views taken on board by a police detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a person's settled set of attitudes or habitual way of thinking.

clue.text: Royal officer completely losing head over queens

indicators.note: over means covering, so one piece goes round the other
the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: very can mean utterly, as in 'the very end'
QU is an abbreviation for queen
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of a queen

explanation.surface: A palace official totally loses his head over queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes V off VERY to leave ERY, and 'over' wraps it round QUER.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer attending a member of the British royal family.
